macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin tops $64,000 as crypto markets rebound ahead of Fed decision
items.summary: Bitcoin rose above $64,000 in Asia trading, while Ether gained and XRP led the majors as investors positioned for the Federal Reserve’s rate announcement. CoinDesk said roughly 70% of traders expected the Fed to hold rates steady.

items.title: Crypto market recap shows mixed prices after recent weakness
items.summary: A market recap showed Bitcoin near $63,799, Ethereum around $1,900, and a total crypto market capitalization of about $2.18 trillion, with sentiment still in fear territory. XRP, Solana, and HYPE were among the notable weekly laggards.

items.title: SEC Chair backs CLARITY Act as crypto market rebound follows Senate uncertainty
items.summary: TradingKey reported that SEC Chair Paul Atkins voiced support for the CLARITY Act, helping crypto prices recover modestly after earlier reports that Senate review of the bill had been suspended. The article said Bitcoin reclaimed the $63,000 area and Ether moved back above $1,900.

items.title: Crypto publication flags major regulatory and policy headlines across the sector
items.summary: crypto.news highlighted regulatory developments including Paul Grewal leaving Coinbase’s legal role before a crucial CLARITY vote, Hong Kong SFC requiring crypto platforms to drop SMS authentication, and the Bank of Korea defending a bank-first stablecoin approach. It also noted Ripple-linked blockchain payment activity gaining attention.

items.title: The Block reports major ecosystem and project developments
items.summary: The Block’s news feed included a Binance Wallet integration for Plume’s yield vault, Cardano governance changes after a wallet exploit, and BNB Chain’s work on a new Layer 1 targeting 2027 mainnet. It also reported European Commission plans to broaden MiCA coverage.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI broadly releases GPT-5.6 and launches ChatGPT Work
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.6 more widely and introduced ChatGPT Work, an AI agent designed to gather context across apps and files and create documents on macOS and Windows. The rollout adds a new workplace automation product to OpenAI’s consumer and enterprise lineup.

items.title: OpenAI discontinues ChatGPT Atlas in favor of the new desktop app
items.summary: OpenAI said it is sunsetting ChatGPT Atlas, its standalone desktop browser, and shifting users toward the new ChatGPT desktop app. The move suggests the company is consolidating product efforts around the main app experience.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.1 to developers in API preview
items.summary: Meta launched Muse Spark 1.1, describing it as a stronger model with more advanced coding capability and a 'step-change' over the first generation. The model is available to US developers through a public API preview.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live voice models for real-time speaking and listening
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release expands OpenAI’s multimodal and voice-focused model lineup.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights governance and safety oversight as major themes in AI development.

items.title: Trump administration lifts restrictions on Anthropic's latest Claude versions
items.summary: The Trump administration removed restrictions on Anthropic’s newest Claude chatbot versions after a weekslong ban tied to cybersecurity concerns. The decision clears the way for broader deployment of Anthropic’s latest models.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Image, its first image generation model
items.summary: Meta released Muse Image, its first AI model for image creation, and made it available through Meta AI, Instagram, and WhatsApp. The launch positions Meta more directly against image-generation offerings from other major AI labs.

items.title: Micron plans more than $250 billion of U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing rising AI-driven demand for memory chips and domestic manufacturing priorities. The announcement underscores the ongoing hardware and infrastructure boom behind AI growth.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: IO Interactive studio closure and layoffs after Xbox pulls funding
items.summary: IO Interactive, the developer behind Hitman and 007: First Light, will close one of its studios and lay off staff after Xbox withdrew funding for an unannounced project. The move adds to a wave of gaming-industry restructuring affecting developers tied to platform-holder funding decisions.

items.title: Microsoft says Game Pass growth has fallen far short of expectations
items.summary: Reports say Microsoft had expected Game Pass to reach 77 million subscribers by now, but it is reportedly only around 30 million. Xbox leadership has acknowledged the strategy has not grown as hoped, making this one of the biggest industry-business stories in the last day.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports are out now on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: Activision has released Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5. IGN notes the ports are available immediately, though the pricing has drawn attention for being high.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced posts a huge Steam player peak
items.summary: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced has reportedly reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam. That is being described as the franchise’s biggest player peak on the platform so far.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks its 10th anniversary with a live event
items.summary: Pokémon Go’s 10th anniversary celebration featured a livestream with announcements and surprises. Coverage indicates Niantic used the event to highlight special in-game activity tied to the milestone.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour shutdown after 7 years
items.summary: Nintendo will shut down Mario Kart Tour this September after seven years of service. No offline version will be offered when the mobile racer ends.

items.title: GTA Online’s next major update is coming next week
items.summary: Rockstar’s next GTA Online update, The Kortz Center Heist, is scheduled for release next week. Fans have already spotted what appear to be Rockstar-related Easter eggs connected to the update.

items.title: PlayStation says physical PS5 game discs will end in January 2028
items.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment has clarified that production of physical game discs for new PlayStation titles will stop in January 2028. After that, new PlayStation games are expected to be digital-only.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: Epic Games has settled its lawsuit against former contractor Hayden Cohen, dropping monetary claims tied to alleged leaks of unannounced Fortnite collaborations. The case had centered on breaches of non-disclosure agreements.

items.title: Xbox and Microsoft investment and studio restructuring continue
items.summary: Industry reporting says Microsoft is increasing investment in MachineGames, while other reports describe broader restructuring across Xbox-related studios. The developments point to continued volatility in Microsoft’s gaming portfolio.
